description: We are three high school students from Kırıkkale, Türkiye. We're building an app that uses NASA Earth data to help farmers in drought-threatened regions choose climate-resilient crops and plan for the future. Our skills: software development, AI, data analysis and design. Our team is complete
summary:
Soil Compass (Toprak Pusulası) is a scientific agricultural decision-support platform and autonomous root-zone mineral delivery rover concept (PUSULA-M1) that fuses live NASA Earth observation data for any global coordinate to project crop suitability in 2026, 2030, and 2040. 

Addressing the challenge of climate-resilient farming, our platform integrates NASA POWER (MERRA-2 and CERES 30-year agroclimatology), NASA SMAP L4 (root-zone soil moisture), NASA MODIS MOD13Q1 (NDVI vegetation index), and NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (SSP2-4.5) climate projections. Powered by SoilCompass-ML—our custom machine learning ensemble (3x Multi-Layer Perceptron + Ridge regression) trained from scratch on 1,257,980 daily NASA observations across 12 global climate stations (achieving R² = 0.968 on unseen stations)—the application performs 50-epoch live in-browser local calibration for any selected parcel to evaluate eight crops, simulate harvest tonnage and water balance, and generate printable A4 agronomic reports.

In regions like Kırıkkale, warming (+0.59 °C/decade) drives atmospheric water demand to 1,161 mm against just 421 mm of rainfall, dropping dryland wheat suitability from 51% to 46% while drought-tolerant red lentil and chickpea maintain 94–95% suitability

PROJECT LINKS & REPOSITORY

Live Web Application: https://strong-bunny-ca138d.netlify.app

Source Code Folder (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/17muT748et6x_MhlQFI0bcS4c-WJV4jQG?usp=sharing

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Soil Compass (Toprak Pusulası) is an interactive geospatial decision-support application and hardware concept that fetches live NASA satellite datasets for any point on Earth to determine how suitable eight strategic agricultural crops will be in 2026, 2030, and 2040.

When a farmer or agronomist opens the platform, it automatically detects their location (via GPS or IP geolocation) or allows them to click any parcel or search any village, district, or coordinate worldwide:

1. Agroclimatological Baseline: It retrieves 30-year (1995–2024) daily and monthly temperature (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), and soil moisture records from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 & CERES).

2. Satellite Soil Moisture & Vegetation Health: It extracts root-zone soil moisture (GWETROOT) from NASA SMAP L4 and 250m vegetation health (NDVI) from NASA MODIS (MOD13Q1) via NASA GIBS satellite pixel decoding and ORNL DAAC services.

3. Climate Projections (2030 & 2040): It combines 30-year observational trends with NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 (GFDL-ESM4, SSP2-4.5 scenario) downscaled climate projections.

4. Biophysical Crop Scoring: Using the Hargreaves radiation equation, the system computes atmospheric evaporative demand (ET0), net water deficit (Precipitation minus ET0), frost days (<0 °C), and extreme heat-stress days (>30 °C), calculating biophysical suitability scores (0–100%) for eight crops: Red Lentil, Chickpea, Drought-Tolerant Barley, Safflower, Wheat, Sunflower, Corn, and Sugar Beet.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. THE PROBLEM SOLVED, BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rising temperatures reduce plant-available soil water even when total rainfall remains constant. In our benchmark analysis for Kırıkkale (Central Anatolia) calculated from NASA POWER records (1995–2024):

• Warming Trend: +0.59 °C per decade

• Precipitation Change (1995–2024): -6.1%

• Projected Root-Zone Soil Moisture Change by 2040: -1.5%

• Annual Rainfall vs. Atmospheric Water Demand (ET0): 421 mm rainfall vs. 1,161 mm evaporative demand (740 mm annual water deficit)

• Dryland Wheat Suitability Score (2026 → 2040): Drops from 51% to 46%

• Red Lentil & Chickpea Suitability Score: Remains resilient at 94–95%

Key Benefits & Impact:

• Replaces guesswork with satellite-backed agronomic planning for any farm globally.

• Economic & Water Simulator: Calculates parcel-specific harvest tonnage and water requirement differences across 10, 50, or 100 decares (or custom hectare inputs), demonstrating up to 38% (20,000 m³ per 100 decares) lower water demand when shifting from wheat to red lentil.

• Printable A4 Field Report Card: Generates a single-page official A4 agronomic report containing parcel coordinates, 30-year NASA climate summaries, 2040 risk metrics, and crop rotation prescriptions ready for field use.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. CREATIVITY & INNOVATION: SoilCompass-ML & PUSULA-M1 ROVER

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A) SoilCompass-ML (Custom Machine Learning Engine Trained from Scratch):

Rather than relying on generic estimates, we trained a dedicated soil moisture and agro-climate model from scratch using 1,257,980 daily NASA measurements across 12 global reference stations spanning diverse climate zones (Kırıkkale, Konya, Imperial Valley, Seville, Kansas, Poltava, Pergamino, Punjab, Saskatoon, Vorkuta, Mato Grosso, and Normandy).

• Architecture: An ensemble average of 3 Multi-Layer Perceptrons (12→16→8→2 architecture) combined with L2-regularized Ridge Regression.

• Input Features (12 Dimensions): Temperature, precipitation, Hargreaves evaporative demand (ET0), solar radiation, extreme heat days (>30 °C), frost days (<0 °C), lagged root-zone soil moisture, and seasonal phase encodings.

• Validation: Tested via strict Leave-One-Station-Out Cross-Validation (LOSO-CV), achieving an aggregate level R² of 0.968 and anomaly R² of 0.627 on completely unseen stations.

• Live In-Browser Calibration: Whenever a user selects a new coordinate anywhere on Earth, SoilCompass-ML performs 50 epochs of live local fine-tuning directly in the browser using that coordinate's 30-year NASA time series.

B) PUSULA-M1 (Autonomous Root-Zone Mineral Delivery Rover Concept):

To bridge digital satellite prescriptions with physical soil restoration, we designed the PUSULA-M1 autonomous solar-powered field rover concept (design specifications):

• Dimensions & Weight: 3.2 × 1.8 × 1.9 m; 1,450 kg empty weight.

• Payload Capacity: 800 kg four-chamber dry mineral hopper (water-retaining zeolite, gypsum, zinc sulfate, potassium sulfate) + 200 L liquid additive tank.

• Field Performance: 3 m working width (6 root-zone injection shanks), 18 decares/hour coverage, ±2 cm RTK-GNSS positioning accuracy, and <0.35 kg/cm² low ground pressure via a tracked drivetrain.

• Energy System: 2.4 kWp solar array + 30 kWh LiFePO4 battery pack.

• Operational Loop: Ingests the Soil Compass satellite prescription map → verifies soil moisture and EC on-site via soil probe → injects water-retaining minerals directly into the root zone → logs application doses for next-season MODIS/SMAP satellite verification.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. TOOLS, LANGUAGES, SOFTWARE & FACTORS CONSIDERED

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

• Languages & Frameworks: JavaScript (ES2023), React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet.js (GIS mapping), Recharts (scientific telemetry charts), HTML5 Canvas (client-side NASA GIBS tile pixel decoding), and Node.js (NEX-GDDP data bridge and ML training pipeline).

• Interactive Query Console: Built-in natural-language and coordinate parser responding in ~76 ms, capable of flying to any named village or coordinate and answering agronomic questions with parcel-specific NASA data.

• Visual Evidence Module ("Why Soil Compass?"): Features interactive full-screen comparisons of 4 real NASA satellite captures (Turkey true-color August 2025, MODIS NDVI, and Lake Tuz drought progression between April and August 2025).

• Factors Considered: Northern vs. Southern Hemisphere seasonal growing window shifts, polar/tundra permanent frost detection (flagging non-arable permafrost regions), separation of real-time weather (Open-Meteo) from 30-year climate baselines (NASA POWER), rainfed vs. irrigated crop thresholds, resilient offline snapshots for instant fallback, and full bilingual support (English & Turkish).
